scenes.say: When I was one month old, I lost about 90 to 95% of my hearing. I’ve worn hearing aids ever since. They made accessibility a lot easier, but they don’t solve every problem.

scenes.say: One problem is that you can’t hear some frequencies of sound, like consonants. That makes it hard to tell these sounds apart: s, f, th, sh, ch, k, p and h.

scenes.say: Soundbook doesn’t replace speech therapy or human support. It’s a tool within speech therapy that makes learning faster, and more fun, for children with hearing loss.

lines: It’s a tool within speech therapy

scenes.say: AI served as an accelerator for research and for exploring different directions, but human judgement was always needed. It showed us many directions, and we judged which ones actually worked in practice.

scenes.say: Claude generated a lot of options quickly: particle stars, glowing orbs, glass sliders, dark and light themes. We asked whether each one would actually work for a five-year-old with a cochlear implant.

v.la: Before: star target over the slider
v.lb: After: a slider between two sounds

scenes.say: The particle star was beautiful, but children couldn’t tell which way to change their sound. So we moved to a simple slider between the two sounds.
